dīductĭo , ōnis, f. diduco,
I.an expanding, separating (very rare; “perh. only in Seneca): ostendit intentionem spiritus velocitas ejus et diductio,” Sen. Q. N. 2, 8, 2 : “in diductione rerum,” in dividing, separating the elements, id. ib. 3, 13, 2 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
